mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the housing market signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply contraction signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% annualized, the combination signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: overheating economy with loose monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the past 3 months, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points, signals robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 5% and UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp in 3 months
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and labor market
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances despite the labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the past quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced demand and lower earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the GDP contraction signal.
